heroHeadline: Iran Hands Over Framework Memo Response as US-Iran Close In on One-Page MOU — Lebanon Ceasefire Fractured by Ghobeiri Strike; Ukraine's Competing Ceasefires Both Collapse
heroSubtitle: On May 7, 2026, Iran was expected to formally hand over its response to mediators on the one-page Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) proposed to end the US-Iran conflict — with Axios reporting the two sides are 'closing in' on a 14-point framework that would declare an end to hostilities and trigger a 30-day negotiating period on the Strait of Hormuz, nuclear limits, and sanctions. The National reported Iran was reviewing the peace plan as its shape solidified. The proposed MOU narrows the diplomatic package compared to Iran's rejected comprehensive 14-point proposal: it defers missile program and proxy force discussions — longstanding US demands — to a later phase, focusing first on ending the war and initiating the Hormuz re-opening process. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner continue leading the US team via Pakistan's back-channel. Meanwhile, the Lebanon ceasefire suffered its most severe violation since April 16 when Israeli warplanes struck Ghobeiri in the southern suburbs of Beirut on May 7 — a densely populated Hezbollah stronghold — reportedly killing a Hezbollah commander, in what Euronews described as the most intense attacks since the ceasefire began. The three-week extension nominally runs to approximately May 14 but is 'in name only' per CBC News analysis; at least 380 have been killed since the ceasefire was declared on April 17, with 2,700+ total fatalities since March 2. In the Ukraine track, both Russia's unilateral Victory Day ceasefire (May 8-9) and Ukraine's counter-proposal (May 5-6) collapsed almost immediately: Russia launched 108 combat drones and three missiles, with Zelensky reporting 1,820 violations by May 6 per Defense News. The 48th ASEAN Summit (May 5-9) confronted Myanmar's civil war with Min Aung Hlaing excluded; analysts called for enforcement mechanisms beyond the toothless Five-Point Consensus. Three major peace tracks are at acute inflection points simultaneously — Iran MOU, Lebanon monitoring collapse, and Ukraine ceasefire failure — making this tracker's scope exceptionally active.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
